summary.text: Earth's internal structure is the way the chemical and physical properties of the solid Earth change with depth, arranged as a series of layers.
By chemistry it has a silicate crust, a mantle and an iron-nickel core; by mechanical behaviour it runs from a rigid lithosphere down to a liquid outer core and a solid inner core.
Although the mantle is solid, its very hot rock can flow over very long timescales, and that convection moves the tectonic plates.

items.prompt: You could drill straight down through a deep ocean floor or through the middle of a continent. Where would you reach the mantle sooner?

options.label: Under the continent, whose crust is denser
Under the ocean, where the crust is thinner
At the same depth in both places
Under the continent, whose crust is thinner

items.explain: Oceanic crust is only 5–10 km thick, while the continental crust is the thicker, less dense part.

items.prompt: The mantle is solid rock, yet its motion carries tectonic plates around. How can that be?

options.label: Ocean currents drag the plates along
The magnetic field pulls on the plates
Hot solid rock can flow over very long times
The mantle is really a sea of liquid magma

items.explain: Although solid, the mantle's extremely hot rock flows over very long timescales, and its convection propels the plates.

items.prompt: No one has ever visited the inner core. What tells seismologists it is solid?

options.label: It transmits shear (sideways) seismic waves
Drill cores brought up solid iron
It is colder than the layers above
Its magnetism holds the metal in place

items.explain: Because the inner core is able to transmit shear waves, it must be solid.

items.prompt: What supplies the heat that keeps Earth's mantle churning?

options.label: Sunlight soaking down through the crust
Friction from ocean tides on the seabed
Burning of deeply buried coal and oil
Radioactive decay plus heat from Earth's birth

items.explain: Decay of radioactive isotopes in the crust and mantle, plus the initial heat from the planet's formation, drives the motion.

items.prompt: Pitch has a viscosity of about 2.3 × 10⁸ pascal-seconds. How does the mantle's resistance to flow compare?

options.label: Over a trillion times stiffer
About equally stiff
Runnier, closer to water
Slightly runnier than pitch

items.explain: The mantle's viscosity is 10²¹ to 10²⁴ pascal-seconds, more than a trillion times that of pitch.

items.prompt: A geologist mentions Earth's lithosphere. Which parts of the planet does that layer include?

options.label: Only the ocean floor rocks
Only the crust itself
The crust plus the uppermost mantle
The entire mantle down to the core

items.explain: Earth's lithosphere is made up of the crust together with the uppermost part of the mantle.

pack.title: What Lies Beneath Your Feet
pack.question: What is Earth made of, layer by layer, from the surface to the centre?

beats.title: What Lies Beneath Your Feet
beats.hook: Thousands of kilometres below you sits a solid ball of iron with a radius about 70% of the Moon's.

beats.prompt: Put these layers in order, from the surface down to the centre.
beats.explain: The crust is the outermost layer, the mantle reaches 2,890 km down, the liquid outer core lies below it, and the solid inner core is innermost.

beats.prompt: Seismologists see shear waves, which shake rock sideways, passing through Earth's innermost layer. What does that tell them about the layer?
beats.explain: Since the inner core is able to transmit shear waves, it must be solid.

choices.label: It is liquid
choices.feedback: Tempting because the layer just above is liquid, but a layer that transmits shear waves must be solid.

choices.label: It is made of rock, not metal
choices.feedback: Shear waves say nothing about metal versus rock; the inner core is mostly iron with some nickel.

choices.label: It is hollow
choices.feedback: A hollow centre would not carry seismic waves through it at all.

beats.prompt: Sort each layer name by the way of describing Earth it belongs to.
beats.explain: The mechanical view sorts layers by rigidity and flow; the chemical view sorts them by what they are made of.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning about moving plates is wrong. Which?

steps.text: The crust and uppermost mantle form the lithosphere.
Below that, the mantle is liquid magma the plates float on.
Convection of the mantle propels the tectonic plates.
Radioactive decay and heat from Earth's formation drive that motion.

beats.explain: The mantle is solid; its extremely hot rock simply flows over very long timescales.

beats.idea: Earth is layered, from a thin crust over a thick, slowly flowing mantle to a liquid outer core and a solid inner core.
